title: To Lower Case
observed_problem_fact: Upper-case ASCII letters map to lower case by a fixed offset; every other character is unchanged
idea_used: Lower-casing ASCII is a per-character offset that needs no table and no copy
m3_applicability: For an ASCII key outside the tr/az/lt languages, String.toLowerCase(locale) is exactly that offset, so the alias probe lowers characters on the fly instead of building convertKey(key). Measured on the D2 experiment body (JMH 1.37, JDK 21.0.9, en): 0 B/op instead of 29 B/op, but containsKey 34.8 -> 74.1 ns and get 68.5 -> 74.5 ns, because the JDK intrinsics of toLowerCase, hashCode and equals beat a char-by-char loop; not shipped
compatibility_limit: Only when neither convertKey nor getLocale is overridden; non-ASCII keys (Kelvin sign, dotted and dotless i, final sigma) and gated locales keep convertKey
read_scope: official problem statement only; no solution, editorial or submission code read or copied

title: Repeated DNA Sequences
observed_problem_fact: Sequences are compared by a hash computed over the characters instead of building substring objects
idea_used: Compute the hash of the transformed sequence while reading it
m3_applicability: The fold hash is 31*h + lower(c) over the key, which equals the String hashCode of the lowered key, so the stored alias hashes match without a lowered copy. Measured on the D2 experiment body (JMH 1.37, JDK 21.0.9, en): 0 B/op instead of 29 B/op, but containsKey 34.8 -> 74.1 ns and get 68.5 -> 74.5 ns, because the JDK intrinsics of toLowerCase, hashCode and equals beat a char-by-char loop; not shipped
compatibility_limit: The spread h ^ (h >>> 16) of the directory is kept

title: Group Anagrams
observed_problem_fact: Strings that belong together are grouped under one canonical key
idea_used: Compare members of a group by their canonical form
m3_applicability: Each alias slot holds the canonical fold of its group; the probe compares the stored fold with the query lowered character by character. Measured on the D2 experiment body (JMH 1.37, JDK 21.0.9, en): 0 B/op instead of 29 B/op, but containsKey 34.8 -> 74.1 ns and get 68.5 -> 74.5 ns, because the JDK intrinsics of toLowerCase, hashCode and equals beat a char-by-char loop; not shipped
compatibility_limit: The single-table merge of alias and payload (brief section 4.2) remains the next phase
